newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-ROMARIO SCORES HAT-TRICK AS BRAZIL HAMMER MEXICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO SCORES HAT-TRICK AS BRAZIL HAMMER MEXICO.

text.p: Striker Romario scored a hat trick as Brazil destroyed Mexico 4-0 with a vintage performance on Wednesday.
Brazil, with 1994 World Cup captain Dunga recalled after a two-year absence, were three goals ahead within 20 minutes as they tore apart a badly-organised Mexican defence.
Brazil had scored four goals in each of their previous friendlies at home to Poland and Chile but their first oppoents had been jet-lagged and the second missing their three top players.
Wednesday's game, against the full-strength CONCACAF World Cup group leaders, was far more meaningful
Midfielder Djalminha set up the first goal in the fifth minute with a through pass to Leonardo, who scored with a right- foot shot.

Seven minutes later, Romario threw himself theatrically over in the Mexican penalty area. His fall fooled almost nobody except the referee who awarded a penalty, which was converted by Romario himself.
Romario added a third five minutes later, when he scored from the edge of the area after the Mexican defence had failed to clear the ball.

Mexico missed two chances to reduce the deficit before halftime, firstly when Brazilian-born striker Zague hit his shot straight at goalkeeper Taffarel and then when Alberto Garcia Aspe struck the post.
Romario completed his hat-trick fifteen minutes from time after being brilliantly set-up by fellow striker Ronaldo.
It was Romario's fifth goal in three games since he made his international comeback this year. Previously, he had been left out for two years by coach Mario Zagallo for lack of enthusiasm.
